parts.answer: The intersection of the closed disc centred at $(0,-2)$ with radius $3$ and the half-plane on the side of the perpendicular bisector through $(1,-3)$ that contains $(0,-2)$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Show a circle centred at $(0,-2)$ - B1. For all marks: accept a scale or dashes representing scale, or labelled points. If scale is on one axis only, allow the same scale on the other. Condone dashed circle and dashed perpendicular bisector.

Show a circle of radius $3$ - B1FT. FT centre not at origin; allow three of four compass directions correct. If no scale, SC B1FT only for the circle.

Show point $(2,-4)$ or midpoint $(1,-3)$ - B1. May be implied by a correct perpendicular bisector; condone $(2,-4)$ on the circle.

Show the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $(2,-4)$ and $(0,-2)$, or of the segment joining $(2,-4)$ and the centre of their circle, going through $(1,-3)$ - B1FT. FT on those positions. It cuts (or would cut) the $x$-axis between 3 and 5 and the $y$-axis between $-5$ and $-3$ if otherwise correct. If no scale, SC B1FT only.

Shade the correct region - B1, dependent on all prior marks. Allow SC B1 if the bisector looks correct and the only error is slight displacement crossing the axes; if no scale, allow SC B1 if relatively correct.

Printed total: 5.
